title: The Four Questions
summary: Akbar tests Birbal with four philosophical questions on life, death, fear, and joy. Birbal delivers four profound answers.
full_text:
During a quiet evening on the palace balcony overlooking the starry Yamuna river, Emperor Akbar posed four deep philosophical questions to Birbal:

'Birbal, you have answered a thousand riddles of statecraft. Now answer me four questions of the human soul:

'First, what is the sweetest thing on earth?

'Second, what is the bitterest thing on earth?

'Third, what is the most terrifying thing on earth?

'And fourth, what is the most courageous thing on earth?'

Birbal bowed and answered with serene clarity:

'Sire, the sweetest thing on earth is truthful praise and sincere affection from those who love us without selfish motive. It nourishes the spirit more than honey or ambrosia.

'The bitterest thing on earth is ungrateful betrayal from a friend or child whom we have nurtured and trusted with our whole heart. It wounds deeper than any poisoned blade.

'The most terrifying thing on earth is a guilty conscience that cannot rest. A tyrant with armies trembles in the dark because his own deeds haunt him like ghosts.

'And the most courageous thing on earth is speaking the truth to a powerful ruler when all others flatter him with comfortable lies.'

Akbar looked at Birbal with deep emotion, recognizing that Birbal had lived every one of those four answers in his service to the empire. Akbar clasped his counselor's hand, thanking him for being the moral anchor of his reign.
